reviewedFrom: Cash method as presented in docs/books-revenue-recognition.md: income when collected (net of refunds, sales tax separate), costs when paid, capitalized purchases separate, and non-income cash flows classified in a bridge. Book-only entries (depreciation, inventory movements, reserves) are listed, not deducted; tax deductibility is a reviewed workpaper adjustment. Pending licensed-CPA review (B16.3). Amounts are integer cents.

two-months-with-bridge.derivation: Invoice 1,080.00 = design 600 + consulting 400 + 8% tax. First month: receipts of 540.00 (half: income 500 split 300/200, tax 40) and 432.00 after a 108.00 credit (income 400 split 240/160, tax 32); the bill is 200.00 paid; owner puts in 500, the loan draws 1,000, the 360.00 truck is bought for cash and depreciated 10.00 (book only); 150.00 moves to savings (nets to zero). Cash: 500 + 1,000 + 540 + 432 - 200 - 360 = 1,912.00 = net income 700 + tax 72 + loan 1,000 + owner 500 - truck 360. Second month (dated today): a 108.00 refund of the second receipt (income -100 split -60/-40, tax -8), the other 100.00 of the bill, an 80.00 draw, a 57.00 loan payment (7.00 interest expense, 50.00 principal), a 0.25 bank fee, 10.00 depreciation (book only). Cash: -108 - 100 - 80 - 57 - 0.25 = -345.25 = net income -207.25 + tax -8 + loan -50 + owner -80. Opening cash is a balance, not movement. A 12.00 insurance premium is paid in the first month (bridged as prepaid) and 1.00 of it is expensed in the books at month end (listed, not deducted), so first-month cash is 1,900.00.

unclassified-refused.derivation: An expense accrued by journal moves no cash and is not depreciation, inventory or a reserve; its later payment by journal moves cash against an accrued liability. Neither has a cash treatment, so the report refuses and says how to fix it rather than guessing the expense.

home-sale.derivation: June: land 60,000.00 bought for cash (bridged as land and homes held), construction 200,000.00 paid (capitalized), a 20,000.00 earnest deposit received and held (bridged). Cash: -60,000 - 200,000 + 20,000 = -240,000. July: the 400,000.00 home closes; the deposit is applied (income, leaving the deposit bridge) and the 380,000.00 wire arrives. Income 400,000, cash +380,000. The 260,000.00 cost of the home sold is relieved from inventory in the books only and is listed, not deducted: whether and when it is deductible is a reviewed tax adjustment.

tax-workpaper.derivation: August cash income is 5,000.00, then 10.00 more posts after the first workpaper is prepared, so book income at review is 5,010.00 (the truck is bought for cash and bridged; its 100.00 book depreciation is listed, not deducted). The accountant's tax depreciation of 100.00 is a reviewed timing adjustment: adjusted income 4,910.00. The no-adjustments replacement reconciles 5,010.00 to 5,010.00 and supersedes the approved workpaper, which keeps its reviewer and notes.
